checkpoints.description: App binary launches under tauri-driver and a WebDriver session attaches to its WebView
The WebView renders a <body> element
The WebView loads a document with a non-empty URL (the platform shell or the offline fallback)
The document exposes a non-empty title
The LLM picker merges on-device (local) models with the provider's cloud models in one availability-ranked list
A not-installed on-device model pulls via the download_model IPC and streams live progress events (real smollm:135m pull against the compiled binary)
Cancelling an in-flight pull returns promptly and the app keeps answering IPC (the no-freeze regression fix)
Clicking a different on-device model while one is downloading shows the 'already downloading' notice (one pull at a time)
A completed pull installs the on-device model (check_ollama_status lists it); the selection UI is covered by odm-06
The nav-bar on-device badge reflects the selected local model
check_opencode_status reports Code readiness (installed / version / config_ready / sandboxed)
install_opencode downloads and installs the pinned opencode release binary (live)
The freshly installed binary is discoverable on the augmented PATH — status reports installed with a version instead of re-downloading forever
Each chat session id gets its own generated workspace under the app-managed workspaces root
A chat keeps the same workspace across calls, persisted in workspaces.json
The folder picker repoints ONE chat at an arbitrary path and leaves other chats untouched
opencode_close / opencode_permission_respond on an unknown id are graceful no-ops
A permission prompt in one chat does not block another chat's turn
The 5-session cap evicts the least-recently-used idle opencode process
The permission prompt renders in the chat that raised it
